newsitem.title: USA: Ford U.S. Q2 marketing costs/revs ratio rises.
newsitem.headline: Ford U.S. Q2 marketing costs/revs ratio rises.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Wednesday its U.S. marketing costs for the second quarter were 9.2 percent of revenues, up from 9.0 percent a year earlier but down from 9.4 percent in the first quarter.
Ford no longer discloses its average U.S. retail incentive figure.
The company reported U.S. combined car and truck market share of 25.6 percent for the second quarter, up from 24.8 percent a year ago and 25.1 percent in the first quarter.

Ford officials said the 0.8 percentage point second quarter market share gain from a year ago was the highest of any automaker in the period. For the first half, Ford's share of the U.S. market was 25.3 percent, unchanged from a year earlier.
In Europe, Ford's combined car and truck market share fell to 11.6 percent from 12 percent in the second quarter. Ford had a 11.4 percent share in the 1997 first quarter.

Ford's share of the Brazilian market was 14.2 percent in the second quarter, up from 9.3 percent a year ago, reflecting sales momentum of new products such as the Ka, Fiesta and Escort cars and Ranger compact pickup truck.
Ford said its worldwide return on sales was 5.3 percent in the second quarter, up from 3.5 percent a year ago.
It said it had a second quarter average car and truck inventory in the U.S. of 59 days, down from 68 a year ago and 62 in the first quarter.
Fleet sales as a percentage of the U.S. sales mix were 28 percent in the second quarter, up from 26 percent a year ago and 27 percent in the first quarter.
